```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
delta   <- 35     # smallest difference of clinical interest (m)
# REVIEW (issue 6, Minor): The SD and the loss come from a hospital registry of 2019–2021; the document does not say how they carry over to the trial, and gives the SD to the app arm without a source
sd_y    <- 90     # SD of 6MWD at 6 months (m)
# REVIEW (issue 1, Major): The evaluable sample size of 55 per group rests on a baseline–outcome correlation that is neither printed nor sourced
rho     <- 0.5    # correlation of baseline and 6-month 6MWD
alpha   <- 0.05
target  <- 0.80
dropout <- 0.20

pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
```

```{r}
#| label: simulate-power
#| include: false
simulate_power <- function(n, n_sim = 200) {
  rejected <- logical(n_sim)
  for (i in seq_len(n_sim)) {
    arm      <- rep(c(0, 1), each = n)
    baseline <- rnorm(2 * n, mean = 380, sd = sd_y)
    outcome  <- 430 + rho * (baseline - 380) + delta * arm +
                rnorm(2 * n, sd = sd_y * sqrt(1 - rho^2))
    # REVIEW (issue 7, Minor): How the supervised physiotherapy is delivered is not stated, and neither the calculation nor the planned ANCOVA allows for outcomes clustering by physiotherapist
    fit   <- lm(outcome ~ arm + baseline)
    t_arm <- coef(summary(fit))["arm", "t value"]
    # REVIEW (issue 2, Major): The simulation tests one-sided at 5% where Table 1 and the text state a two-sided 5% test, and every printed number comes from the one-sided rule
    rejected[i] <- pt(t_arm, df = fit$df.residual, lower.tail = FALSE) < alpha
  }
  mean(rejected)
}

set.seed(20260108)
grid        <- seq(40, 100, by = 5)
power_raw   <- vapply(grid, simulate_power, numeric(1))
# REVIEW (issue 9, Minor): Figure 1 plots a running maximum of the simulated power, not the estimates its caption names
power_curve <- cummax(power_raw)
# REVIEW (issue 3, Major): The chosen sample size and its 81.5% power rest on one 200-trial estimate per grid point and on taking the first point to reach 80%
n_evaluable <- grid[which(power_curve >= target)[1]]
power_at    <- power_curve[grid == n_evaluable]
# REVIEW (issue 4, Major): The dropout allowance multiplies by 1.2 instead of dividing by 0.8, so 66 randomised per group leave 52.8 evaluable at the stated 20% loss
n_rand      <- ceiling(n_evaluable * (1 + dropout))
```

```{r}
#| label: ttest-comparison
#| include: false
n_ttest <- ceiling(power.t.test(delta = delta, sd = sd_y, power = target)$n)
```

*Demonstration document. The study, its sources and all numbers are invented.*

Version 1.0, 15 September 2026.

# Study design

DEMO-TKA is a planned single-centre, randomised, controlled, parallel-group
superiority trial in adults undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Within
two weeks after surgery, participants are randomised 1:1, in permuted blocks of
variable size, to app-guided home exercise (intervention) or to supervised outpatient
physiotherapy (control), each delivered over 12 weeks.

# Primary endpoint and estimand

The primary endpoint is the six-minute walk distance (6MWD, in metres) at 6 months
after surgery, measured with a standardised protocol by assessors blinded to the
allocation. The pre-operative 6MWD is the baseline value.

<!-- REVIEW (issue 5, Minor): The estimand names no intercurrent events, so it is not stated which effect the 35 m difference refers to, nor how death or inability to walk at 6 months enter -->
The primary estimand is the difference in mean 6MWD at 6 months between app-guided
home exercise and supervised physiotherapy in adults undergoing primary TKA who are
eligible for the trial. All randomised participants are analysed in the group to which
they were allocated.

# Planning values

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|:--------------------------------------|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Smallest difference of clinical interest | 35 m | Agreed with the investigators (steering committee, 3 June 2026) |
| SD of 6MWD at 6 months | 90 m | Hospital TKA registry, 2019–2021 (internal report) |
| Significance level | 5%, two-sided | |
| Power | 80% | |
| Loss to follow-up at 6 months | 20% | Hospital TKA registry, 2019–2021 (internal report) |
| Allocation ratio | 1:1 | |

: Planning values. {#tbl-planning}

# Sample size

The primary analysis is an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) of 6MWD at 6 months with
treatment group and baseline 6MWD as covariates. Because adjustment for baseline
increases precision, we estimated power by simulation. For sample sizes of 40 to 100
evaluable participants per group, in steps of 5, we simulated 200 trials under the
planning values in @tbl-planning, fitted the ANCOVA to each and counted the trials in
which the treatment effect was statistically significant at the two-sided 5% level
(@fig-power).

```{r}
#| label: fig-power
#| fig-cap: "Estimated power by number of evaluable participants per group (200 simulated trials per sample size). Dashed line: 80% power; dotted line: chosen sample size."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.4
par(mar = c(4.2, 4.4, 0.8, 0.8))
plot(grid, power_curve, type = "b", pch = 19, ylim = c(0.5, 1), las = 1,
     xlab = "Evaluable participants per group", ylab = "Estimated power")
abline(h = target, lty = 2)
abline(v = n_evaluable, lty = 3)
```

The smallest sample size with at least 80% power is `r n_evaluable` evaluable
participants per group (estimated power `r pct(power_at)`). For comparison, an
<!-- REVIEW (issue 10, Minor): The unadjusted t-test comparison prints a typed 94 per group, where the printed planning values give 105 -->
unadjusted two-sample *t*-test would require 94 participants per group.

Allowing for 20% loss to follow-up, we will randomise `r n_evaluable` × 1.2 =
`r n_rand` participants per group, `r 2 * n_rand` in total.

# Analysis

<!-- REVIEW (issue 8, Minor): The 20% allowance holds for an analysis of all randomised participants only if the lost are handled as missing at random, which the document does not state -->
The primary analysis is the ANCOVA described above. The handling of missing outcome
data and any sensitivity analyses will be specified in the statistical analysis plan.

# Software

Simulations were run in `r R.version.string`. The simulation code and the random seed
are part of the source of this document.
